newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks end week higher, volumes rise.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks end week higher, volumes rise.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's stock market ended the week to Thursday higher in active trade triggered by good second quarter company results, the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) said.
The all-share index closed 2.98 percent higher at 169.68 points from 164.77 points the previous week.
Of the 57 shares traded during the week, 52 rose, four fell and one was unchanged.
BFA put trading value at about 1.18 billion riyals ($310 million) up from last week's 934 million riyals.
The banking and the industrial sectors dominated trading value with 38 percent and 24 percent of the total respectively.
A total of 5.6 million shares changed hands, up from 3.9 million shares a week earlier.
Al-Baha led the week's gainers, rising four riyals to 65 riyals and SABIC gained five percent to end the week at 439 riyals from 418 riyals.
Saudi Hollandi Bank closed at 527 riyals from 517 last week and Saudi Cable at 112 riyals from 110.
Saudi Real Estate Company (SRECO) closed four riyals lower at 135 riyals from 139 riyals and Food Products lost 1.9 percent to 196 riyals.
